title: Working with Teammates in Five Time Zones
meta: B2 · 约 280 词 · 场景：跨时区协作

sections.heading: 1. The Hidden Cost of the Overlap Hour
paragraphs: Our team has people in Bangalore, Singapore, Sydney, London and San Francisco.
On a map, that looks impressive.
In a calendar, it looks like a ==puzzle== with no clean solution.
The usual answer is to find one overlap hour and put every meeting there.
But someone always pays for that hour, and it is usually the same people: the ones joining at seven in the morning or ten at night.
Over time, they stop speaking up, and the team starts losing their ideas without noticing.
**Time zones are not just a scheduling problem; they are a fairness problem.**
If one office always __bears the cost__, ==resentment== builds quietly, even on a friendly team.
People rarely complain about it directly, but you will see it in shorter answers and cameras that stay off.
That is why the ==arrangement== matters as much as the agenda.
paragraphs_zh: 我们团队的人分布在班加罗尔、新加坡、悉尼、伦敦和旧金山。
放在地图上，看着挺唬人。
放进日历里，就是一道怎么拼都拼不齐的拼图。
通常的做法是找一个大家都在线的重叠时段，把所有会都塞进去。
但总有人要为这个时段买单，而且通常是同一批人：早上七点或者晚上十点进会的那些。
时间一长，他们就不怎么发言了，团队也在不知不觉中丢掉了他们的想法。
时区不只是排会的问题；它是公平的问题。
如果总是同一个办公室承担代价，哪怕团队氛围再好，不满也会悄悄积累。
大家很少会直接抱怨，但你会从越来越短的回答、一直不开的摄像头里看出来。
所以会怎么安排，和议程本身一样重要。

sections.heading: 2. Rotate, Record, Hand Off
paragraphs: First, ==rotate== the inconvenient slot.
If the weekly sync is painful for London this month, move it so that Sydney __takes a turn__ next month.
People accept a bad time much more easily when they can see it is shared.
Second, record every meeting and write a short summary of the decisions.
Someone who could not attend should be able to __catch up__ in five minutes and still give input ==asynchronously== before anything is final.
Third, end each day with a ==handoff== note.
Three lines are enough: what I finished, what is blocked, and what the next person can __pick up__.
**A good handoff note means the work keeps moving while you sleep.**
Done well, five time zones stop feeling like a ==burden==.
The project becomes a relay race, with progress happening __around the clock__ instead of waiting for one shared hour.
paragraphs_zh: 第一，把难受的时段轮换起来。
如果这个月的周会对伦敦很痛苦，下个月就挪一挪，让悉尼轮一次。
大家一旦看到苦是轮着吃的，接受一个糟糕的时间就容易多了。
第二，每个会都录屏，并写一份简短的决策纪要。
没能参会的人应该能在五分钟内跟上进度，并且在事情拍板之前，还能异步给出意见。
第三，每天下班前写一份交接说明。
三行就够了：我做完了什么，卡在哪里，下一个人可以接着做什么。
交接写得好，你睡觉的时候活儿也在往前推。
做好了，五个时区就不再是负担。
项目会变成一场接力赛，进度二十四小时不停，而不是干等那一个共同的小时。

gist.q: 作者说“只找一个重叠时段开会”有什么隐性代价？
gist.a: 总是同一批人在清晨或深夜付出代价，久而久之他们不再发言，团队悄悄失去他们的想法。

gist.q: 作者把时区问题重新定义成什么问题？
gist.a: 不只是排期问题，而是公平问题；某个办公室一直承担成本，怨气会悄悄积累。

gist.q: 文中的三个做法是什么？
gist.a: 轮换不方便的时段；会议录像并写决策摘要，让缺席者能异步参与；每天结束时写三行交接（完成了什么、卡在哪、下一个人能接什么）。

prompts.q: 你们组的周会一直定在新加坡下午四点，对旧金山同事来说是深夜。你在会上提出轮换时间，30 秒。
prompts.ref: One process point before we close. Our weekly sync has been at four in the afternoon Singapore time for almost a year, which means Mike has been joining after midnight. That's not fair to him. I'd like to rotate the slot every month, so each office takes a turn with the bad time. I'll send a proposed schedule today.
prompts.ref_zh: 散会前说一个流程上的事。我们的周会快一年都定在新加坡时间下午四点，这意味着 Mike 一直是过了午夜才进会。这对他不公平。我想每个月轮换一次时间，让每个办公室都轮着承担难受的时段。我今天把排期方案发出来。

prompts.q: 下班前给伦敦同事发一条语音交接，30 秒说清：完成了什么、卡在哪、他可以接什么。
prompts.ref: Hi Emma, quick handoff before I log off. I finished the retry logic and all the tests are green. I'm blocked on the config change, because I still don't have access to the production settings. If you have a moment today, could you pick up the code review from Arun? Everything else can wait until I'm back tomorrow morning.
prompts.ref_zh: Hi Emma，下线前快速交接一下。重试逻辑我写完了，测试全绿。配置变更那块卡住了，因为我还是没有生产环境配置的权限。你今天有空的话，能不能把 Arun 的 code review 接过去？其他的都可以等我明天早上回来再说。

words.ex: Planning the on-call rotation across four offices is a real puzzle.
Always scheduling demos at night for one team will create resentment.
The current arrangement works for Singapore but not for London.
We rotate the meeting time every month so no office always loses.
Please review the design asynchronously and leave comments by Friday.
A clear handoff saved us a full day on the incident.
Late-night calls shouldn't be a burden on the same people every week.
Why should the Sydney team bear the cost of our planning mistakes?
With three regions, we can support customers around the clock.
